newsitem.title: TURKEY: Floods and forest fire hit Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Floods and forest fire hit Turkey.

text.p: Floods paralysed low-lying parts of Istanbul on Tuesday and emergency services used boats to rescue people cut off by the rising waters, witnesses said.
In southwest Turkey, fire services used aircraft to fight a forest blaze near a popular Mediterranean holiday resort, Anatolian news agency reported.
It said the fire covered an area of around a thousand hectares (2,500 acres) and was approaching two residential areas, several km (miles) from the resort of Marmaris.
In Istanbul, police and fire services worked together in rescue operations overseen by governor Kutlu Aktas in the city's rundown Kagithane district.

"The rain came suddenly at night. We were so afraid that we could not sleep. We are still scared," said local resident Fatma Kesen as emergency workers navigated boats across flooded streets towards stranded workers.
Two workers were rescued after clambering onto a mechanical digger and a police boat saved a dog trapped amid the waters.
Local officials said work was continuing on assessing the damage caused by the muddy flood water which inundated many city streets after heavy rains which began on Sunday night.
"Around 300 houses were flooded. The value of the damage is being evaluated," governor Aktas was quoted as saying by Anatolian news agency.
Thirty-two workers at a chemical factory in Kagithane were stranded overnight after a failed attempt by armoured personnel carriers to rescue them.
Twenty of the 32 escaped from the factory by wading up to their necks through the water, Anatolian said. A further forty workers were rescued by boats from a factory in the same area.
Flooding caused damage elsewhere in Turkey.
One bridge was destroyed, hundreds of houses were flooded and electricity was cut off in parts of Zonguldak province on the Black Sea due to heavy rains, Anatolian said.
It said the train line between Ankara and Zonguldak was closed to traffic because of the flooding.

Turkish authorities have sent initial emergency aid of five billion Turkish lira ($31,000) to the eastern province of Agri in response to a weekend flood which claimed the lives of eleven people, the agency said.
